All node-link claims remain hypotheses or inferences until nickel inclusion in Indonesia's export framework and contract/FX-routing effects are verified from primary regulation, company filings, and trade-flow data. Layer 1B expanded the universe around the regulation/logistics/working-capital chokepoint rather than only physical nickel mining. The strongest reference anchor is Vale because PT Vale Indonesia is a direct Indonesian nickel producer. The underfollowed lane points to non-Indonesian nickel-development alternatives and second-order HPAL input exposure: Lifezone Metals for Tanzania nickel plus hydrometallurgical processing, Canada Nickel for Canadian nickel-sulphide restart/development optionality, and Hawkins for sulfuric-acid distribution exposure tied to HPAL feedstock constraints. These are research candidates only; the Indonesia export-rule inclusion of nickel and direct contract impacts still require primary-source verification.
